title: Rich Chiaroscuro Devotional Portrait
positive: A rich chiaroscuro devotional portrait of the goddess Durga in the Bengali tradition, painted in the manner of a classical oil painting, serene and exceptionally beautiful, facing the viewer directly and centered in a wide panoramic frame. A single warm golden light falls from above and slightly left, sculpting her face and jewelry, while the wide left and right sides of the frame dissolve into deep velvet shadow. Her figure fills the frame from just above her crown to her feet, the crown complete and uncut. Her face is large and finely rendered: two matching natural eyes with dark irises, level and symmetrical, gazing gently at the viewer, and a small vertical third eye in the center of her forehead, clearly separate from the natural eyes. Tranquil expression, softly closed lips. Deep crimson silk with gleaming gold zari borders, an opulent gold crown, necklaces, earrings, armlets and bangles, with restrained diamond accents glinting in the light. A softly glowing gold halo emerges from the darkness behind her head. Ten arms, five from each shoulder region, spread in an orderly symmetrical fan, every arm with a natural elbow, wrist and graceful hand, each hand holding one distinct object in the light: trident, sword, discus, conch, bow, arrow, bell, axe, shield, coiled noose. A single healthy lion with realistic anatomy lies calmly at her feet, its two matching eyes catching the light. Velvety blacks, glazed oil texture, quiet reverence.
